mouse: Structure: hover a row boundary, then click. Held Option/Alt temporarily reveals the same targets.
keyboard: ⌘/Ctrl+Enter below; add Shift for above. Enter keeps its native cell meaning.
rule: Focus the new expression. Insert in a named lexical scope, never at an alignment spacer. A draft row is an edit, not a proven no-op.

mouse: Rows: drag anywhere on a binding row. Slot stays in a candidate position; Float follows the pointer. Double-click a cell for editing or values.
keyboard: Focus the row; Space picks up, ↑/↓ chooses a destination, Enter drops, Escape cancels.
rule: Refactor offers checked destinations. Free edit permits scope/dependency changes but always produces valid structural syntax. The final result is not an ordinary movable let.

mouse: Choose Copy in the structure commands; later compare Shift-drag with the deck’s left-then-down gesture.
keyboard: Row command “Duplicate below”; then use the same keyboard pickup.
rule: Fresh syntax IDs and a fresh binder; redirect references inside the copied subtree only. Copying evaluation is not generally a refactor.

action: Create a reference from a binding
mouse: Connect: pull a flexible wire from a binder to a hole. Word-center anchors; optional hover links. Drag an existing use to move or unplug it in Free edit.
keyboard: “Insert reference” at the caret opens in-scope bindings; arrows and Enter choose. Study: pick a binder, Tab to a hole, Enter.
rule: Resolve by binder identity and lexical context, not matching spelling. Never silently capture a different same-named binding.

mouse: Structure: drag an indicated expression to a typed slot; explicit Copy variant.
keyboard: Native structural cut/copy/paste; command “Move expression” can reuse destination picking.
rule: Old Furl moved single words, not arbitrary Hazel subtrees. Expand to subterms only with source-slot and capture rules.

mouse: Pull the selected expression to an earlier binding boundary.
keyboard: Command “Extract binding”; reuse Hazel’s refactor chord where available.
rule: Old implementation only extracted a literal immediately above its own row. Hazel ExtractLet/Explode can supply broader candidates.

mouse: Drag an unresolved occurrence to the boundary above its row.
keyboard: At that occurrence, command “Create binding above”.
rule: Keep the occurrence; create a binder of that name with a hole. Check for collisions.

mouse: Old editor: click between words or drag from its word palette. Proposed: native Hazel completion or a compact structure menu.
keyboard: Use Hazel typing and completion; Tab moves through new holes.
rule: Do not reimplement a second token editor. Old Space made a new word; that mapping should not replace Hazel’s input model.

mouse: Rows / Connect: drop a row or existing reference outside the code canvas. Preview deletion before release; never remove at pickup.
keyboard: Backspace on a completely empty row; ⌘/Ctrl+Shift+Backspace requests row deletion. Backspace/Delete on a focused use. ⌘/Ctrl+Z restores.
rule: Populated rows and uses require Free edit; blank draft cleanup works in every policy. Result stays. Escape, invalid in-canvas drops and policy changes cancel. Old Furl used a trash collection; do not inherit its destructive pickup.

mouse: Click a cell normally; double-click in Structure mode. Binder/use highlighting helps follow references.
keyboard: Existing Furl arrows retain column targets. Tab should visit structural targets only when explicitly entering that layer.
rule: Old Shift+↑/↓ swaps rows; retain native Shift-selection in text. Do not globally steal it.

mouse: Select a contiguous row range, then Group; compare Alt-drag / left-then-up as an expert gesture.
keyboard: Row selection + “Group into block”; name the resulting binding.
rule: A nested let changes scope. Reject or explicitly export bindings still used outside the chosen block.

mouse: Structure: drag the top or bottom comb endpoint across row boundaries.
keyboard: Focus an endpoint; arrows preview moving it one boundary, Enter commits.
rule: The endpoints change lexical extent, not CSS height. Show escaping uses and keep required exports.

mouse: Pull the top comb boundary downward; crossed definitions become parameter candidates.
keyboard: “Abstract leading rows”; choose a range, preview parameters and call, then commit.
rule: Create a function plus a call supplying old definitions. Preserve evaluation order; update all affected uses. Start with one tuple parameter.

mouse: Structure: drag parameter slots or use an endpoint command.
keyboard: Commands plus directional parameter navigation; reuse the same transform planner.
rule: Hazel patches known calls and rejects bare escaping uses in relevant transforms. Adding argument holes is an edit; reordering needs evaluation-order checks.

action: Turn a binding into a match
mouse: After a refutable pattern is complete, show a fork preview; accept on the comb.
keyboard: Commit pattern, then command “Branch on this pattern”.
rule: Deck proposes automatic creation. Start with an explicit acceptance so intermediate typing does not rearrange the editor; add a fallback hole without claiming semantic equivalence.

mouse: Structure: click or pull the match fork right. In normal mode it keeps its current view action.
keyboard: At the branch handle, command “Add branch”; Tab enters its pattern/body.
rule: A branch is a pattern plus a body, not a let row. Place a new branch before a catch-all or use a coverage witness.

mouse: Drag a whole branch column by its comb handle in Structure mode.
keyboard: Pick up a branch handle; ←/→ previews, Enter commits.
rule: Case order is semantic. Refactor requires disjointness or a stronger proof; the branch currently uses a conservative disjoint-pattern test.

mouse: Pull a definition toward an occurrence; preview whether it is copied or consumed.
keyboard: Commands “Inline binding” / “Inline this use”; use Hazel FeedLet and InlineLet.
rule: Distinguish one use from all uses. Preserve precedence, capture avoidance, evaluation behavior, and comments.

mouse: Refactor drag pauses at a dependency; offer a preview carrying the necessary rows.
keyboard: At a blocked move, choose “Move with dependencies”.
rule: Make the larger operation explicit. Do not silently turn a small reorder into a helper extraction.

action: Extract a helper at a scope boundary
mouse: Pull a dependency group beyond a function ceiling, then accept a helper preview.
keyboard: “Extract helper”; review free variables as parameters and rewritten uses.
rule: Hazel LiftFunction handles a specific contiguous dependency run and enclosure shapes, not every arbitrary selected Furl region.

mouse: Select an expression, choose “Expose intermediates” / “Inline intermediates”.
keyboard: Use Hazel Explode / Implode commands; bind an optional chord after testing conflicts.
rule: Introducing let-bound intermediates is a source refactor. Merely furling existing syntax is a view change; keep the two actions distinct.

action: Inspect / specialize a call or case
mouse: Select a live call, then inspect a substituted view. A separate command applies a source rewrite.
keyboard: Value arrows navigate; explicit “Step here” / “Bind argument” are source commands.
rule: A rewrite justified by one sample is not valid for every input. A temporary inspection must not mutate source, history, or persistence.

action: Furl, unfurl, switch branches and calls
mouse: Existing comb clicks, all/one branch choice, and selected-value arrows.
keyboard: Existing cross-cell arrows and Ctrl+Alt+←/→ for branch inspection.
rule: View operations stay available outside Structure mode and never become undoable syntax edits. Windows refactor chord conflicts with branch navigation: use row/branch-focused arrows first.

mouse: Existing binding/expression/value toggles; later add types, environments, assertions, and trace pinning.
keyboard: Focus a toolbar control; Space toggles it. Commands can restore a hidden caret column.
rule: Extra value columns are invocation views, not duplicated source. No new code row for controls.

mouse: Preview a candidate while dragging; settle identified rows on release.
keyboard: Keyboard moves get the same preview and settled state; reduced-motion gets immediate transitions.
rule: Old editor used UID-based 150ms position transitions. Do not animate syntax by interpolating token text or save intermediate states.

mouse: Click a microphone at the focused cell, dictate, correct a small transcript, then insert.
keyboard: Focusable record/stop and accept/cancel controls; ordinary typing remains available.
rule: One insertion transaction at a retained source target. A late transcript cannot land in a different cell. Service choice remains open.
